questions.q: What is the sum of all interior angles of any quadrilateral?
questions.a: The sum is 360 degrees. A wrong answer like "180 degrees" shows the student is confusing quadrilaterals with triangles.

questions.q: Can a quadrilateral be a rectangle if it does not have four right angles? Why or why not?
questions.a: No, a rectangle must have all four angles equal to 90 degrees by definition. Answering "yes" indicates the student does not understand that properties define the name of the shape.

questions.q: A quadrilateral has three angles measuring 80°, 100°, and 80°. What is the measure of the fourth angle?
questions.a: The fourth angle is 100° (360 - 260 = 100). If a student gets this wrong, they likely failed to subtract correctly from 360 or forgot the total sum rule.

questions.q: How is a rhombus different from a square, even though both have four equal sides?
questions.a: A square must have 90-degree angles, whereas a rhombus does not require its angles to be 90 degrees. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks side length is the only defining property of these shapes.

questions.q: Is it correct to call a square a type of rectangle? Defend your answer.
questions.a: Yes, because a square satisfies all properties of a rectangle (opposite sides parallel, all angles 90°), plus it has the extra property of equal sides. If a student says "no," they don't understand the hierarchical nature of geometric classifications.

questions.q: Draw a figure that is a quadrilateral but is neither a parallelogram nor a trapezium. Describe its properties.
questions.a: A kite or a generic irregular quadrilateral. The answer should explain that it has four sides but lacks parallel sides. A poor answer would be drawing a triangle or a shape with more than four sides.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A ______ is a closed two-dimensional shape formed by four straight line segments (sides) and four interior angles, where the sum of these interior angles is always 360 degrees.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever looked at a school playground or a ______ frame and noticed how many different four-sided shapes there are?

Fill in the blank: A quadrilateral is a closed two-dimensional shape formed by four straight line segments (sides) and four interior angles, where the sum of these interior angles is always ______ degrees.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify, name, and categorize quadrilaterals based on their specific properties (parallel sides and equal angles) and calculate a missing angle using the sum-of-angles rule.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Have you ever looked at a school ______ or a window frame and noticed how many different four-sided shapes there are?
